documents.title: Responsible Use of AI at URI
documents.summary: An ITS page setting principles (transparency, accountability, fairness, privacy), data-security standards and role-specific expectations for educators, students and researchers. It does not set a default for coursework AI use; students are told to follow instructors' policies.
documents.stance_why: The page "embraces" AI but sets no rule on what is allowed in coursework; it tells educators to "clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students" and students to "Follow instructors’ AI policies", so the decision is handed to instructors (delegates).

units.why: The opening sentence states the university's overall position: URI "embraces" AI as "a powerful tool for teaching, learning, research, and innovation". It is a default welcoming stance for everyone, a general principle (phase general, informs), so P02 fits better than P87 (benefits) because it states URI's own posture, not a list of benefits.
units.anchor: embraces artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful tool for teaching, learning, research, and innovation
units.frag_start: The University of Rhode Island (URI) embraces

units.why: The same sentence says AI must be used "securely, ethically, and responsibly" and the page sets out "URI’s standards and practices"; this is a preamble of purpose and principles, i.e. an institution-wide framework (P56).
units.anchor: ensuring AI is used securely, ethically, and responsibly

units.why: Under Guiding Principles, Transparency says to "Clearly disclose when AI tools are used". It is a disclosure rule for all users, phrased as a principle (should), so P24 (disclose AI use) fits.
units.anchor: Clearly disclose when AI tools are used to create content or make decisions.

units.why: The Accountability principle includes "Validate the accuracy of AI outputs", a verify-output duty (P31); the separate duty to take responsibility is coded as its own unit.
units.anchor: Validate the accuracy of AI outputs
units.policy: Validate the accuracy of AI outputs

units.why: The second half of the Accountability principle says users must "take responsibility for their use" of AI, matching P29 (own what you use or submit); chosen over P116 because it names accountability concretely.
units.anchor: take responsibility for their use
units.policy: Users take responsibility for their use of AI outputs

units.why: The Fairness and Inclusivity principle says "Mitigate biases and ensure AI systems respect diversity and equity"; it names bias and equity concerns, so P53.
units.anchor: Mitigate biases and ensure AI systems respect diversity and equity.

units.why: The Privacy and Security principle says to "Protect sensitive and institutional data from misuse"; a data-protection rule, P50.
units.anchor: Protect sensitive and institutional data from misuse and unauthorized access

units.why: Key Resources lists a "Guidelines for the Secure and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence" document that gives guidance on transparency, accountability and compliance. The passage directs readers to further guidance and informs rather than commands, so P115.
units.anchor: comprehensive guidance on AI transparency, accountability, and compliance with accessibility, privacy
units.frag_start: Guidelines for the Secure and Ethical
units.policy: Guidelines for the Secure and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence provide guidance on AI transparency, accountability, and compliance with accessibility, privacy, and intellectual property standards

units.why: Under Policies and Standards, Data Security and Privacy says URI "enforces" these standards and tells users to follow the Data Classification Guidelines "to avoid exposing restricted or sensitive information"; data protection, P50 (must, since URI states it enforces the standards).
units.anchor: to avoid exposing restricted or sensitive information.
units.policy: Follow URI’s Data Classification Guidelines to avoid exposing restricted or sensitive information

units.why: The Accessibility standard says to "Ensure all AI tools comply with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)"; it concerns accessibility of AI tools, P97.
units.anchor: Ensure all AI tools comply with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)
units.policy: Ensure all AI tools comply with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)

units.why: The Prohibited Data Use standard says to "Avoid inputting private or restricted data" such as PII or patient records into public AI tools like ChatGPT. It is a data-privacy ban rather than a ban on pasting assignment material, so P50 with a fit note, not P20 or P49.
units.anchor: Avoid inputting private or restricted data
units.frag_end: into public AI tools like ChatGPT.
units.policy: Avoid inputting private or restricted data, such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or patient records, into public AI tools like ChatGPT
units.fit_note: Bans entering PII or restricted data into public AI tools; P50 is about protecting data and preferring vetted tools, not specifically about a prohibition.

units.why: Data Handling Awareness warns that "data entered may be transmitted to third-party servers", asking for caution; an awareness statement about data exposure, P50.
units.anchor: Be cautious when using AI platforms, as data entered may be transmitted to third-party servers.

units.why: Disabling Data Logging says to "disable history and logging features" where possible so information is not stored or used for training; a privacy practice, P50.
units.anchor: disable history and logging features to prevent information from being stored
units.policy: Where possible, disable history and logging features to prevent information from being stored or used for AI training without consent

units.why: Intellectual Property Compliance says to "Respect copyrights" and avoid confidential data in AI systems without protections. Copyright is the lead concern, so P52; the confidential-data part overlaps P50 (already coded above).
units.anchor: Respect copyrights and avoid using confidential data in AI systems
units.policy: Respect copyrights and avoid using confidential data in AI systems without appropriate protections in place
units.fit_note: Also says to avoid confidential data in AI systems without protections, which is a privacy rule (P50).

units.why: Under Education and Training, URI invites people to "Attend sessions on responsible AI use tailored for faculty, staff, and students"; AI-literacy workshops for the whole community, so P70 (not P63, which is faculty only).
units.anchor: Attend sessions on responsible AI use tailored for faculty, staff, and students.

units.why: The Accessibility Resources bullet says to "Learn how to make AI tools and outputs more inclusive" through URI accessibility programs; accessibility of AI outputs, P97.
units.anchor: Learn how to make AI tools and outputs more inclusive
units.policy: Learn how to make AI tools and outputs more inclusive through URI’s accessibility programs

units.why: Understanding AI Functionality says to "understand how it works, what data it collects, and how it handles that data" before using any AI platform. It asks users to assess a tool before use, P117.
units.anchor: Before using any AI platform, take the time to understand how it works
units.policy: Before using any AI platform, users take the time to understand how it works, what data it collects, and how it handles that data

units.why: The Educators guideline says to "Incorporate URI’s guidelines into course design"; instructors are tied to the university guidance, so P77 (follow existing university policy).
units.anchor: Incorporate URI’s guidelines into course design
units.policy: Educators incorporate URI’s guidelines into course design

units.why: The same Educators sentence says to "clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students", a duty to make expectations explicit, P09 (it does not require a syllabus statement by name, so a fit note).
units.anchor: clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students
units.policy: Educators clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students
units.fit_note: Says to communicate acceptable use to students but not specifically in the syllabus.

units.why: The Educators sentence also says to "disclose when AI was used to create course materials"; the rule is about disclosure of AI-made course materials, P48.
units.anchor: disclose when AI was used to create course materials
units.policy: Educators disclose when AI was used to create course materials

units.why: The Students guideline begins "Follow instructors’ AI policies", sending the decision to instructors and making students responsible for following them, P78.
units.anchor: Follow instructors’ AI policies

units.why: The Students guideline says to "properly attribute AI-generated content", a disclosure and citation duty, P24.
units.anchor: properly attribute AI-generated content

units.why: The Students guideline says to "avoid using AI in ways that breach URI’s Student Code of Conduct"; it ties AI use to an existing conduct policy, P77.
units.anchor: avoid using AI in ways that breach URI’s Student Code of Conduct
units.policy: Students avoid using AI in ways that breach URI’s Student Code of Conduct

units.why: The Researchers guideline says to "Consult with your department and comply with regulations when using AI tools in research"; AI in research, P62.
units.anchor: comply with regulations when using AI tools in research
units.policy: Researchers consult with their department and comply with regulations when using AI tools in research, particularly for handling sensitive or proprietary data

notes: Only uri-responsible-ai was included in the collect file; uri-grad-ai (a thin news post) is screened exclude and was not coded. Many units use should/must for principles phrased as imperatives.
